chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abū Jamīlah Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who gouged out the eye of a man whose sight was gone while the eye itself remained in place, he said: “Upon him is one quarter of the indemnity (diyah) of the eye.”

key_terms.الْعَيْنِ: the eye for which the indemnity is calculated
key_terms.دِيَةِ: financial indemnity prescribed for bodily injury
key_terms.ذَاهِبَةً: gone, meaning its sight had departed
key_terms.عَيْنَ: the eye as the injured bodily organ

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on gouging out an eye that had already lost its sight?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning injury to an eye whose sight had already been lost, though the eye itself remained physically present. It states that gouging out such an eye entails one quarter of the diyah of an eye, reflecting a graded assessment of bodily injury in Islamic jurisprudence.
